newsitem.title: USA: CME hog futures end mixed, pork bellies lower.
newsitem.headline: CME hog futures end mixed, pork bellies lower.

text.p: CME hog futures closed mixed, and pork bellies lower with wide price swings noted in February bellies in the closing minutes.

News of lighter-than-expected hog marketings Tuesday and light marketings Wednesday at interior Iowa and southern Minnesota points fueled light buying in October hog futures, traders said. October set a contract high of 60.675 cents a lb during the session.

USDA reported actual Iowa/southern Minnesota hog marketings Tuesday at 89,000 head, well below 105,000 estimated. It also estimated that 100,000 head were sold there Wednesday versus 106,000 a week ago. The light marketings were attributed to farmers' focus on corn and soybean harvesting rather than on selling hogs.
Pork belly futures were actively traded late with the February contract moving in a wide range in the closing minutes, traders noted.
Market-on-close buying by Prudential Securities erased a large share of February's losses, floor sources said.

Traders attributed much of February's gyrations to technical influences. The day's high of 79.800 cents was at chart resistance points and prompted early selling. Later February rebounded after falling to support near 77.20 cents.
Hog futures closed down 0.475 cent a lb to up 0.300 cent with October up 0.150 at 60.075 cents. Pork bellies were down 0.350 to 0.900 cent with February off 0.350 at 78.525 cents.
